verdicts.text: It hath been watched a long while, and hath given nothing away.
The scribes set out ink and parchment, and it sat upon the parchment.
It keepeth its own counsel, and its counsel keepeth it.
What it knoweth, it knoweth; and what it thinketh of thee, it will not say.
It was seen once at a window, and the matter hath been discussed ever since.

natures.text: It is not that it hath nothing to say. Thou hast not earned it.
Of the hours the Cat spendeth watching, no record is kept, for it leaveth none.
It cometh when it pleaseth, not when it is called. No longer do the scribes call.
The Owl is said to see everything. The Cat seeth as much, and maketh less of it.
Nine lives are attributed to it. The Cat hath shewn us but part of one.
Though it speaketh little, it is free with its regard, and many a creature hath felt its approval without once hearing its voice.
It neither speaketh nor applaudeth, but only watcheth, which is the oldest of the arts.
